title: Your AI games look generic because of one mistake
author: Diligent-Hat-6509
selftext:
If you ask AI for a genre, you get the average of that genre. That's why so many AI games look the same.

For my last game I started with one sentence, a feeling instead of a genre: "a cabin, hot tea, and a blizzard outside the window." AI built everything (ChatGPT for references, Claude in Blender, Codex in Unreal), and I only made the decisions, in 4 steps:

1. \*\*Goal:\*\* one sentence. A feeling, not a genre.

2. \*\*Reference:\*\* make the feeling visible. Skip images that are pretty but not yours, and keep the happy accidents. ChatGPT randomly added a tiny red figure, and he became my main character.

3. \*\*Rules:\*\* turn the feeling into rules AI can follow, like "soft, never sharp" or "only shelter is warm".

4. \*\*Check:\*\* every decision has to pass one question: "does this feel like sitting in a cabin with tea, watching the storm?"

When the first trees came out too sharp, I didn't have to explain anything. My rule says soft, so everything got rounder.



What's your trick for avoiding the generic AI look?
